title: fleet-quota-rebalancer-slippage-accounting-and-graceful-debit
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed that burst credits and reserved quotas sometimes sit idle on underloaded tenants while other tenants temporarily hit SLA throttles. This PR implements a fleet-level quota rebalancer that (1) proactively redistributes short-term burst budget across compatible tenants within a reservation class, and (2) accounts for slippage and debt so that rebalancing does not cause sudden regressions for donors or recipients.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Introduces a new "quota rebalancer" background controller that computes transferable credit windows and issues grace-limited transfers at configurable intervals.
- Adds slippage accounting: when credits are transferred, both donor and recipient receive an amortized slippage ledger entry to smooth the impact across subsequent allocation windows.
- Implements graceful-debit behavior for recipients: if downstream load drops, the rebalancer drains amortized credits over a configurable decay period instead of immediate revocation.
- Extends utilization reporting with amortized-credit-aware metrics: reported util% now includes an "effective utilization" value that factors in temporarily borrowed budget and shows donor/recipient deltas.
- Exposes new autoscaler knobs: min_headroom_ratio, slippage_tolerance_pct, transfer_window_secs, debt_decay_secs, and max_concurrent_transfers.
- Adds a new telemetry export for "transfer events" (transfer_start, transfer_commit, transfer_revert) with contextual tags for reservation_class, donor_tenant, recipient_tenant, and reason.
- Regression and integration tests for stability under bursty traffic and during rolling upgrades.

Why it's safe: Transfers are conservative by default (slippage_tolerance_pct=3, transfer_window_secs=300, max_concurrent_transfers=2). All transfers are reversible by policy within the debt_decay_secs window and emit audit entries so operators can trace state changes. The rebalancer only operates within the same reservation class and respects tenant-level hard caps.

Files/areas changed (summary):
- runtime/fleet/rebalancer.go: new controller and reconciliation logic.
- runtime/fleet/ledger.go: amortized slippage ledger and decay logic.
- runtime/autoscaler/config.go: new knobs and validation.
- telemetry/metrics/exports.go: transfer events and effective_utilization gauge.
- api/v1/reservations.proto: added TransferEvent proto and new fields on ReservationStatus.
- docs/ops/rebalancer.md: operator guide and recommended alerts/dashboards.
- test/integration/rebalancer_burst_test.go: load scenarios and assertions.

Testing and results:
- Unit test coverage added for ledger math and decay (ledger coverage ~92%).
- Integration load test (100 tenants, stochastic burst model) shows 18% reduction in SLA throttles for high-demand tenants during 15m peak windows, with median donor impact <1.5% latency regression.
- CI: initial perf benchmark flagged a small race in ledger expiry; fixed in second commit and all checks passed on final run.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated off by default.
2) Enable in canary fleet for 48h with transfer_window_secs=600 and slippage_tolerance_pct=1.
3) Observe effective_utilization and transfer_* telemetry; ensure donor_loss_p50 < 2% and no transfer_revert spikes.
4) Gradual ramp to 30% of fleet then full rollout.

Monitoring and alerts to add (docs/ops/rebalancer.md):
- Alert if transfer_revert_rate > 0.5% over 5m.
- Alert if average debt_per_tenant > reserved_capacity * 0.2 for > 10m.
- Dashboard panels: transfer event timeline, donor/recipient latency delta, amortized debt heatmap.

Related work: ENG-1187 (fleet headroom adjustments), ENG-1199 (utilization telemetry revamp).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Perf bench (rerun after fix)
- [x] Docs and operator guide
- [x] Feature gate and default off

Notes: This design intentionally avoids cross-reservation-class transfers to reduce blast radius. We plan a follow-up PR to add a soft-scheduling hint so the admission layer can prefer donors with lower p95 latency for transfers.
